title: August and the Cipher
premise: Mara Zhou, a night-shift dispatcher whose anonymous letters have quietly solved three 'accidents,' is drawn into the town's founding mystery when the coffin of beloved founder August Hale is exhumed and found empty. Following a cipher hidden in Hale's own letters to her late grandmother, Mara discovers the founder faked his death to escape a crime he committed—and that her grandmother helped him vanish, trading her silence for the taxi company Mara now works for. As the tide recedes to reveal what Hale buried on the flats, Mara must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the last person who ever loved her; she publishes the cipher's answer but withholds the body's location, closing the case on her own terms and finally stepping out of the shadows.
about_author: Odile Zhou is a former harbor-town radio operator who spent a decade listening to other people's emergencies before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who solve things from the edges of the room.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A night shift at Harborline Dispatch: we meet Mara through the voices she routes, the logbooks she annotates, and the anonymous letters she's mailed about three deaths the police closed. Emotional beat: competence as camouflage—Mara is brilliant and deliberately unseen.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Erosion on the tidal flats exposes a corner of a coffin; the town exhuming founder August Hale for a centennial reinterment finds it empty. Mara, listening on the scanner, hears the panic before the news breaks. Beat: dread—the past has her address.

chapters.title: The Man Who Built the Town
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with archival excerpts. She researches Hale: philanthropist, lighthouse benefactor, buried with honors in 1968. A librarian mentions Hale corresponded with a 'Miss Wei'—Mara's grandmother. Beat: a cold finger of connection.

chapters.title: Letters to Miss Wei
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In her grandmother's steamer trunk she finds forty years of letters from Hale—affectionate, then coded, then desperate. The final letter is pure cipher. Beat: grief and fascination entwined; her grandmother loved a mystery.

chapters.title: Detective Voss Calls
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Detective Voss, half-grateful and half-suspicious of Mara's anonymous letters, warns her off the empty coffin—and quietly asks for her eyes. Beat: the dangerous thrill of being seen by someone who matters.

chapters.title: Frequency 4
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss works the exhumation angle: who had access, who benefits. He notices Mara's name on the taxi company's founding papers—signed by Hale himself. Beat: suspicion with an undertow of respect.

chapters.title: The Cipher's Shape
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She cracks the outer layer: a route cipher keyed to taxi routes Hale helped map. The plaintext is a confession fragment—Hale writes of 'the boy in the boathouse' and 'what Wei agreed to carry.' Beat: vertigo; the inheritance is complicity.

chapters.title: The Company's First Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Harborline's 1951 ledger shows Hale funding the taxi company the year after the boy's drowning—an 'accident' Mara recognizes from her first solved case's pattern. Beat: the cases were never separate; they were echoes.

chapters.title: Old Harbor, New Eyes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, walking the town. She interviews the last living boathouse hand, ninety-three and sharp, who remembers Hale's rage the night the boy died. Beat: the founder's marble face cracks; grief for a town's false idol.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her dispatch locker is searched; a letter she never sent appears in the police tip line. Someone inside Harborline is watching her. Beat: paranoia—the invisible woman is being made visible against her will.

chapters.title: The Successor
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss identifies the watcher: Ruth Hale, the founder's great-granddaughter and Harborline's current owner, who commissioned the exhumation expecting an empty coffin. Beat: the hunter was bait all along.

chapters.title: Ruth
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth wanted proof the family legend was true—that August walked into the sea. She offers Mara partnership: find the body together, restore the name, share the truth. Beat: temptation of an ally who understands obsession.

chapters.title: The Second Cipher
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The inner cipher unlocks with her grandmother's maiden name as the key: coordinates on the tidal flats and a date—the coming equinox low tide. Beat: the deadline is set by the moon.

chapters.title: What Wei Agreed To
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reconstructed from letters: Wei, Hale's lover, drove the getaway the night of the drowning and kept his secrets for the company. Mara confronts the possibility her whole life was built on hush money. Beat: identity shaken to the studs.

chapters.title: The Tip That Wasn't Anonymous
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. A tip accuses Mara's grandmother of the drowning itself—forged, Voss realizes, but it forces the case open publicly and puts Mara under official scrutiny. Beat: the machinery she once used now turns on her.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Mara and Ruth's alternating POV. At the equinox low tide they reach the coordinates and find a sealed strongbox—Hale's full confession and evidence—just as someone's flashlight sweeps the flats. Beat: triumph curdling into pursuit.

chapters.title: The Third Person on the Flats
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The watcher is Harborline's dispatch supervisor, who has spent decades guarding the company's secret to protect his own father's role in the cover-up. He wants the strongbox and the tide is coming in. Beat: fear, physical and mortal.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, high tension. In the rising water Mara outthinks the supervisor, using the dispatch network—every taxi on the channel—to bring Voss to the flats. The supervisor is taken by the tide's edge and rescued, broken. Beat: her invisible skills save lives in the open.

chapters.title: The Confession Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hale's confession confirms the drowning, the flight, the coffin filled with ballast. Voss must decide whether a dead man's crimes can be prosecuted and whether Wei's silence was crime or mercy. Beat: the law meets the gray.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss chooses to close the case as solved—Hale named, the living accomplices aged beyond prosecution—and offers Mara credit. She declines the byline. Beat: the quiet cost of the truth; love offered, duty honored.

chapters.title: Reinterment
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The town reburies an empty coffin with a new stone that tells the truth; Ruth reads Hale's confession aloud. Mara stands in daylight, named, unmasked. Beat: mourning the myth, keeping the man.

chapters.title: The Dispatcher
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, coda. Mara takes over Harborline openly, keeps the cipher framed on her wall, and mails one last anonymous letter—solving a fresh hit-and-run—because some versions of herself she'll never fully give up. Beat: resolution with a heartbeat; she is seen now, and chooses what remains hidden.
